Hello! I'm after some advice on how to tackle a project. I have written basic firmware for a few microcontroller devices which were quite simplistic (ATtiny and ATmega with simple IOs). I have a fairly good grasp of C and microcontroller hardware, but I'm coming from a PC programming background (object oriented Java, etc.), and I'm having some trouble adapting to programming microcontrollers.

I've purchased a few books on embedded systems, AVR, and C, but they all tend to be reference material and explain things in detail without covering much on program design and architecture. What I mean is, advice and best practices on putting a larger more complex firmware together. I have seperate C modules for my ADCs, TWI, SPI, UART, etc. What's the best way to stitch everything together that is robust and maintainable?

I've put things together, but it feels like I'm breaking modularity in some ways (maybe this is just the way MCUs are programmed), and my code base starts to feel like I have to many variables linking different modules together. Without experience, I'm second-guessing the architecture/flow of the code.

Are there any good resources that cover this? Not necessarily language or brand specific, but something that can help me better adapt to putting the entire firmware together?
Good resources for programming system architecture?

I'm still after suggestions, but thought I might share what I've found useful so far:

Here's a good video about embedded operating systems: https://youtu.be/akNSxGyoFQg

Check out a book called Making Embedded Systems that covers this sort of thing at the beginning. Chapter 2 is literally titled "Creating a System Architecture". My roommate and I just bought copies of this game for PC and it's been a lot of great fun so far. However, we are having multiple issues that I was hoping to get some info on.

Whenever I open the game, at the bottom of the screen it says that I am offline, even though I am playing online multiplayer. My wins on my vehicles are not being recorded either (they all say 0 still). Could these be related issues?

The other issue that actually affects our gameplay is what seems to be buggy voice communication. We have each separately had issues where one of us could communicate, but the other could not be heard. Resetting the game a couple times didn't work, but they did come back after setting my audio options back to default. My roommate and restarted his game and now his mic wasn't working. I told him to try what I did, but it didn't fix it for him. Has anyone had issues similar to this? Or heard of any patches coming to fix it? This game is so much more fun when you can talk with your teammates.
[PC] Loving the game so far, but running into a few issues.
Hopefully someone can help you out. I personally have the game for PS4 so I'm of no use, but I hate seeing these types of posts with no replies!
I'm on PC and have the same issues. Haven't tried Voice yet though.

So after doing some more reading I've answered most of my initial questions. The "you are offline" is because Psyonix's stat tracking servers were turned off due to an unexpected popularity at the launch of the game. They will be turning these back on once they are certain it won't affect the stability of the game. This is why your wins with each car don't track, and I think this might also by why ranking seems to be buggy as well.

For the mic issues, it seems that the game just doesn't have very good voice communication. Since we are playing on Steam, we just used Steam Voice Call as a workaround and it is much better quality than what the game provides at it's best.

I didn't look at my settings the first couple days, but when I did, I realized that the default sets everything to on and Highest Quality. Turning these down greatly increased the performance of the game. Also we both used XInput to use PS3 controllers, and the game is so much easier to control with them. Now with full, clear voice comms, higher frames per second, and controllers, the game is even more enjoyable. I recommend these changes to all PC users. Hope this helps someone.
